description: We are an aunt-and-nephew creative duo. By pairing a young explorer’s boundless imagination and passion for space with his aunt’s research expertise and guidance, we brought this interactive story to life.
summary:
In this heartwarming and imaginative story, a curious kid and his aunt begin their cosmic journey of discovery from their own rooftop. Together, they explore the wonders of Europa, Jupiter’s mysterious icy moon, imagining what life forms might swim within the vast, hidden ocean beneath its frozen crust. As they discuss about the Europa's hidden ocean, the conversation shifts from distant stars back to their own home. Ultimately, the aunt uses the magic of space exploration to teach her nephew a vital, grounded lesson. 
Powered by verified data from NASA and other trusted institutions, this project illustrates a creative way to teach complex space science to everyone.
details:
The Lunar Whisper is a digital storytelling experience for children and families. Through 4 chapters, the story connects Europa's hidden oceans to presence of life and importance of water in our lives. There is also an emphasis on flood prevention and understanding of global warming's impact on the life of common man.

It makes complex science simple for the children. It teaches that water is life on Europa AND on Earth. It gives 5 practical promises children can do today.

Its aim is to make children feel that space science is their story, not a far-away story. Also, to build a habit of water-saving and flood preparedness. And to inspire the next generation to build a probe to Europa - but first protect the water we already have.

We wrote and illustrated the story as an interactive digital storybook using Netlify app, and AI-assisted (Nano Banana 2, ChatGPT) illustration for the visuals. No coding or hardware was needed. The project is a storytelling and science-communication experience.

We link a moon ~770 km away, to the river in Pakistan. We turned Webb into "an ear that listens" and NASA's SWOT satellite into "NASA's flood watch".

Our team considered accuracy, age-appropriateness, and local relevance. We checked that NASA does not directly warn villages - it shares satellite data that local agencies use. We kept the language simple, hopeful, and respectful of the real Pakistan floods. We focused on prevention, not fear.

- Team Phantom Rovers.
